p0: P0-1 propagate the renderer -> trusted verifier/BROKER service -> challenge-authority split through the ENTIRE normative contract. rev-28 declared the nine-role table but the topology diagram + §2.1 (peer-auth/caller/nonce/return-path) + §4.10(g) (governed_turn_execute) + §6.1/§7.1 still named ONE in-process desktop/Tauri principal. rev-29: a global terminology binding resolves every trusted-actor 'desktop'/'backend' reference to the broker service (never the renderer); the topology diagram is three-tier; the challenge-authority IPC allowlists ONLY the broker UID and DENIES the renderer/login UID; ONLY the broker supplies create-pending facts/request_nonce/issue and receives the signed challenge; PreparedGovernedTurnV1B + receipt DB + pinned manifest + final verification + accepted-output persistence live ONLY in the broker; governed_turn_execute is a broker-service operation and the Tauri command a THIN proxy carrying only {conversation_id, agent?}; a NORMATIVE renderer<->broker IPC schema (peer auth, frame limits, timeout, replay/idempotency, errors) is defined; ONLY the broker emits the committed UI-safe result. All stale normative references removed (historical Appendix A keeps the old model).

P0-2 include the broker and challenge-authority in the TCB integrity floor (§2.5). rev-29 expands TCB_ARTIFACTS to include the trusted verifier/broker + desktop-challenge-authority executables, their config/policy, service/unit files, IPC policies, broker pinned-manifest config, and every loaded library/plugin; both services require root/TCB ownership + non-writability (mode/ACL/group/ancestor) + start-time SHA-256 pin + fail-closed verify_tcb_integrity() + service UID/SID verification + peer-auth policy verification; 7 negative tests (login-writable/modified broker or authority binary/config, writable ancestor, wrong owner/SID/UID, fake broker cannot create/persist/display Verified) => governed mode DISABLED.

P0-3 define FD survival across BOTH exec boundaries (§2.7, §4.7). rev-29 splits the contract: the RECORDER (before execve(launcher)) maps the 3 inputs + output to FDs 3-6, dup2/dup3s, explicitly CLEARS FD_CLOEXEC on 3-6, redirects 0/1/2 to inert endpoints, close_range(7,~0), execve with fixed argv + empty env; the LAUNCHER (before fexecve(executor)) verifies EXACTLY FDs 3-6 (mode/inode/type/offset/store-binding), re-confirms/clears FD_CLOEXEC on 3-6, rejects any unexpected FD incl. 0/1/2, opens the executor image O_NOFOLLOW|O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC, performs the locked privilege drop, fexecve with ONLY 3-6 surviving; 7 integration/negative tests (survive recorder->launcher; survive launcher->executor; tiny executor reads 3 inputs + writes FD6; CLOEXEC before either boundary => fail closed; unexpected stdio/extra FD => fail closed; every failure => no receipt/evidence/record).
